title: Constructibility and dense-open vanishing of the normalization mono cokernel
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $f:X	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ a separated finite-type morphism with $\dim X\le1$, and $X$ reduced [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\ell$ a prime such that $R=\Lambda/(\ell)$ is finite as a set. Let $
u:X'	o X$ be finite and surjective, let $V\subseteq X$ be a dense open over which $
u$ is an isomorphism, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open with pullback $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $
u':U'	o U$. For any monomorphism $\alpha:j_!\underline R_U	o
u_*j'_!\underline R_{U'}$ of small-etale sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules (extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]), $\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ is constructible [def-constructible-constructible] and its inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] on $V$ is zero.

source.place: Proof sketch: cokernel constructibility and vanishing over the isomorphism locus; arbitrary-mono generalization justified by finite stalks

proof.text: The schemes X and X′ are Noetherian: X is a finite-type scheme over a field, and X′ is finite over X. The constant sheaves with value R=Λ/ℓΛ are finite locally constant because R is cyclic over Λ, hence constructible. Extend their stratifications by the closed complements of U and U′. Extension by zero is constructible by [lem-fin-extension-by-zero]. Finite direct image is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-constructible-noetherian]: apply the finite-stalk argument to the underlying finite set sheaf, with the induced module operations on each stratum. The sheaves remain killed by ℓ, so all module operations factor through the finite ring R; refine the finite-set trivialization to trivialize the finitely many R-operations. This justifies the passage to constructible Λ-module sheaves without requiring Λ itself to be finite. Both comparison terms are therefore constructible. Their cokernel is constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]; its recorded Lean cokernel theorem works over any ring, not only a finite one.

Over V, where ν restricts to an isomorphism, finite base change [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange], constant-sheaf pullback [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], and [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero] identify the two comparison terms with the extension-by-zero constant R-sheaf on U∩V. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves the mono α and its cokernel. Inside U∩V it is an injection between two finite sets of the same cardinality |R|, hence a bijection; outside U both geometric stalks are zero by [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Thus the restricted morphism is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Inverse image preserves cokernels, so the restriction of cokernel α to V is zero. No chosen-diagonal hypothesis on α is needed, precisely because R is finite.
